summary: Set 116 Session 3 of 3, "Ten gates to three" -- the set-terminal session. THE RULING, IMPLEMENTED AND ATTESTED: the operator's 2026-08-10 gate ruling was presented as an education-mode brief and re-attested at the moment of implementation (decisions.jsonl, authority=human, rubric_line=verification-reduction), because reducing verification sits inside the decision-rights hard carve-out and decision_journal refuses to write it under AI authority. Ten close-out checks are now THREE gates (verification_integrity, uat_walk_recorded, test_run_fresh), TWO transactional preconditions (working_tree_clean, pushed_to_remote -- they protect the WRITE, not the ceremony), and FIVE advisory checks that run, print, and cannot refuse (activity_log_entry, next_orchestrator_present, change_log_fresh, checklist_posted, verification_method_vocabulary). NOTHING WAS DELETED: every demoted check keeps its predicate, message and tests, and a test asserts that. gate_checks.ADVISORY_CHECKS is the executable form of the table and is_blocking_check() the single predicate every consumer asks; GateResult carries a `blocking` field so gate_results says which kind each row was, and [WARN] replaces [FAIL] on a demoted failure. GATE (c) REPAIRED: pytest and mocha carried expensive=False -- and `expensive` is the flag deciding whether test_run_fresh has an OPINION, not a claim about the clock -- so the once-per-session rule never governed the suite that cost the time (Set 112 S3: 15 runs, 186 minutes, unremarked). All three layers are now expensive, and the full run moved from Step 5 to Step 8, after remediation, because Step 7 remediation IS a code change and the old instruction was unsatisfiable rather than merely ignored. TWO DEFECTS THE TESTS CAUGHT THAT READING DID NOT. (1) Removing the close backstop's vocabulary early-out was wrong: the ruling falsified the REASON that skip gave, not its conclusion, since an unknown verification_method still has no corroboration path -- restored with corrected reasoning. (2) Demoting change_log_fresh turned a clean refusal into a CRASH: _flip_state_to_closed required change-log.md to be PRESENT before calling a session the last one, a mirror unreachable while the gate refused first; once the gate warned, a final session without one wrote status:in-progress over an all-complete sessions[] and raised SessionStateInvariantError. The redundant condition is removed and the regression asserts the resulting STATE, not merely that the close succeeded. The generalisation is L-069-1 read backwards: demoting a gate is not a local change -- find every sibling of the GUARANTEE you are removing, because while the gate blocked, those siblings were unreachable and therefore untested. VERIFICATION: round 1 (discovery, 2-lens fan-out, gpt-5-6-sol both lenses, anthropic excluded, $0.786) returned VERIFIED from BOTH lenses with zero Critical/Major. Five nits; all five fixed, because three were documents written this session that stated something false about the code beside them. Both lenses converged independently on two: "a docs-only session owes nothing" is FALSE under ai_router/ (covers is a path PREFIX, not a file type -- narrowing it to exempt docs folders was considered and REJECTED because it would make the gate skippable by putting code in a docs-named folder; both sides of the boundary are now pinned by tests), and --force was never inside "every close" (it runs verification_integrity alone; correct and older than this ruling, so documented rather than changed). Per-nit record: s3-nit-dispositions.md. SET-TERMINAL DELIVERABLES: change-log.md, the REQUIRED path-aware critique, and the Step 9 review. Suites of record taken after the last code change, per the ordering this very session ships: pytest 3850 passed / 5 skipped (301.05s) and Playwright 36 passed (12.1m, owed because close_session.py and session_state.py are both on its covers list). OPERATOR CONSTRAINT recorded mid-session: parallelism capped at 8 pending Set 117's fix for an OS-resource bug; every run here used -n 8, while pytest.ini still declares -n auto. That disagreement is a named residual for Set 117, which is already authored.
